Can you triage ASAP? This is customer-impacting for Payments.

Karthik / team — preliminary findings from the first 30 minutes of collection:
- Observed SNAT port pool exhaustion on the Dedicated Egress NAT instance serving AcmePay's pool; ephemeral port utilization hit ~98% during the spike window.
- Conntrack table shows a large number of short-lived TCP entries (many in CLOSE_WAIT / TIME_WAIT).
- Firewall logs (partner-managed) show a burst of SYN retries from the AcmePay side followed by retries from our side as connections were being dropped.

Attached packet-capture has multiple simultaneous new TCP handshakes followed by RSTs. This pattern aligns with short connection lifetimes + aggressive client retries (retry storm).

Short-term mitigation I recommend (we can apply now):
1) Increase SNAT port allocation for the AcmePay SNAT pool (double ephemeral port range mapping).
2) Add temporary SNAT session pinning (keep mappings longer for their subnets).
3) Suggest customer reduce connect-and-close pattern (they indicated a canary with small, short-lived sessions).

I'll push a change to expand ephemeral mapping and monitor for 15 minutes; will share logs.

-Priyom
Solutions Engineer

Thanks Priyom — good catch. A few operational notes and next steps:
- We did a routine kernel backport last week for the Dedicated fleet in us-west-2 but no config changes to conntrack defaults. That said, conntrack sizing was borderline for very high short-lived connection workloads; I will temporarily bump the table size for the AcmePay host pool.
- We'll increase the SNAT ephemeral mapping and open an emergency rule to extend their port range (will coordinate with Diego at CloudCo for peering NAT side).
- Recommend activating the hosted fallback route for this customer's route policy for the next 24h to drain pressure on Dedicated while we stabilize. That requires a config change to routing-policy/acmepay which I can push with approved rollback.

I will apply the SNAT and conntrack updates in this order: 1) bump conntrack size, 2) increase SNAT mapping, 3) enable hosted fallback. Each step will be monitored for errors and latency.

I'll also capture bridgelogs and attach.

-Laura
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
